_comment: Consumed by scripts/growth-ops/scheduler.mjs via .github/workflows/growth-ops.yml. Cadence numbers grounded in SaaS-launch-playbook research — see automation-setup.md for sourcing and what's solid data vs. rule-of-thumb. Edit campaign_start before your first real run; it drives every phase boundary below.

twitter._comment: Off by default — no secret configured. Same phased cadence as Bluesky/Mastodon if you opt in; costs real money per post (see automation-setup.md).

reddit._comment: 1x/week is the one cadence number multiple sources agree on for avoiding spam-flag risk, and only across DIFFERENT subreddits — never the same one repeatedly. Bounded to 4 curated weeks (month 1); after that this channel goes silent rather than looping the same posts. Each content_calendar item below is genuinely distinct copy tailored to that subreddit's norms, not an identical cross-post — see automation-setup.md for why that matters.

content_calendar.title: Built a tool that audits your site the same way your CI audits your code — dogfooding it on our own site right now (60/100, ouch)
content_calendar.body: Spent the last few months building RankCLI — SEO + GEO (AI-search-citation) checks that run in CI and open a PR when something's fixable, instead of another dashboard alert. Free tier runs entirely local via MCP, no signup. We're eating our own dog food publicly: rankcli.dev currently scores 60/100 on its own audit. Happy to answer anything about the build or take feedback on the free tier.

content_calendar.title: Every 'AI SEO' tool is a $29-$2000/mo dashboard for marketing teams. We built the CI-native one instead — launch pricing inside
content_calendar.body: Researched the GEO/AI-visibility space before building RankCLI and found the same product everywhere: a monitoring dashboard, priced for marketing budgets, that tells you whether ChatGPT mentioned your brand. None of them run in CI or ship a fix as a PR. We're launching with founding pricing — first 100 Pro subscribers at $19/mo instead of $29, locked in for as long as you stay subscribed. Free tier (MCP, local, no signup) is genuinely unmetered since it runs on your own API key, not our infra.

content_calendar.title: Cloudflare started blocking 'mixed-use' AI crawlers by default on ad-hosting zones (Sep 15, 2026) — here's a free check for whether that silently hit your site
content_calendar.body: If you're on Cloudflare and haven't explicitly configured robots.txt rules for GPTBot/ClaudeBot/PerplexityBot, your AI-crawler access now depends on an account-level default you may not have looked at. Built a free check for this into RankCLI (`npx @rankcli/mcp-server`, no signup, runs locally in Claude Code/Cursor/etc.) alongside the usual technical SEO stuff — Core Web Vitals, structured data, security headers. Curious if others have hit this.

content_calendar.title: The data behind 'AI SEO': being crawled isn't the win, being cited is (35%/91% more clicks when you are)
content_calendar.body: Google's own numbers: organic CTR on AI-Overview queries has fallen from ~1.8% to under 1% since mid-2024, but brands actually cited in an AI answer get 35% more organic clicks and 91% more paid clicks than uncited brands, even when both rank the same underlying position. That gap is the whole thesis behind a CI-native SEO/GEO tool I built (RankCLI) — treating AI-citation readiness as a lint target instead of a marketing metric. Wrote up the full research behind the positioning if anyone wants the source data, otherwise happy to talk shop on the GEO checks specifically.
